provenance.instrument: Perkasie Borough Zoning Ordinance of 2012 (Chapter 186 Zoning, Ord. No. 963 of 2-9-2013, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 PE0952, Borough of Perkasie, Bucks County (186-5 'Decision': Court of Common Pleas of Bucks County, 186-14 Bucks County Department of Health). District use lists and lot, yard, coverage and height figures are text in 186-20. The Table of Uses by District and the maps are PDF attachments and were not opened. Floodplain rules are in Chapter 94. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 12-15-2025.' New Laws: 'There are currently no known new laws for this Code.'
checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. Each district permits listed uses 'and no other' (186-20A(1) to 186-20L(1)). The I-3 Airport Industrial District lists no dwelling and no special exception use (186-20L). Accessory uses are those 'customarily incidental to a permitted use and not normally conducted as an independent principal use' (186-18H(1)). The 'accessory dormitory' is housing for faculty or students of a school on a five-acre lot (186-18H(2))

'Residential conversion: The conversion of an existing building into two or more dwelling units or the conversion of an accessory building into one or more dwelling units' is a special exception in R-1A, R-1B, R-2, R-3, A, C-1, C-2, I-1 and I-2 (186-18B(6), 186-20). A converted detached house must keep the look of a detached house with a single front entrance. Added entrances go on the side or rear, outside stairs on the rear wall, and there may be no major structural change to the outside (186-18B(6)(a), (b))

Twin dwellings are permitted by right in R-1B, R-2, R-3 and C-2, and duplexes (one unit over the other) in R-2, R-3 and C-2 (186-20). A two-family lot is 9,000 sq ft and 4,500 sq ft per unit in R-2 and R-3, 8,000 and 4,000 in C-2, and 15,000 and 7,500 for a twin in R-1B. 186-18B(2)(c) also gives two-family lot figures by bedroom count (3,600 to 4,500 sq ft, Ord. No. 1051), and which table governs a district lot is not settled

The single-family tables set a 'minimum lot area per dwelling unit' equal to the lot minimum (13,500 sq ft in R-1A and R-1B, 7,000 in R-2 and R-3, 6,000 in C-2). Whether a conversion needs that area for each unit is not settled. For it: 'The lot area and yards required for any new building or use shall not include any part of a lot that is required by any other building or use' (186-21), and 186-24 sets lot area and lot area per dwelling unit. Against it: in the Town Center Overlay a conversion into three or more units in R-2 takes 'The standards for any other structure or use in § 186-20C except for minimum lot area' and its own 3,000 sq ft per unit (186-20J(3)(b)), which suggests that elsewhere a conversion takes the 'Any Other Principal Structure or Use' table, with no figure per unit. Read per unit, a two-unit conversion in R-2 would need 14,000 sq ft, or 9,000 sq ft if read as a two-family dwelling

Accessory buildings may stand in the side and rear yards 5 ft from the lot lines and 5 ft from the house, at most 15 ft tall (186-27A, 186-41). 'An accessory structure shall not be located between the front yard setback line and the front facade of a house' (186-27C). The R-3 single-family table reads an accessory height of '1.5 feet', which looks like a typing error for 15 ft

Parking: 2 spaces for a single-family house. A two-family or converted unit needs 1 space (efficiency or one bedroom), 1.5 (two bedrooms) or 2 (three or more). 'Any fraction of the next highest number shall be counted as one', and for residential uses spaces inside garages do not count (186-61C, 186-62D, G)

No zoning permit is issued until the Bucks County Department of Health approves water and sewage, and where public water or sewer is available a connection permit from Perkasie Regional Authority comes first (186-14A, B)

Floodplain (Chapter 94): 'Within any identified floodplain area, any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited', unless a variance is obtained under Article VIII, and then the lowest floor must be at or above the regulatory flood elevation (94-22). New construction means a structure begun on or after March 16, 2015, with any later improvements to it (94-37). Work on an older building is an improvement, prohibited when it reaches 50% of the market value, and smaller work is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible (94-32, 94-33). Nothing new within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of a watercourse in an AE area unless DEP's regional office issues a permit (94-17B(1)(b), 94-33F). An accessory structure in the floodplain may not be used for human habitation (94-22E(1)). The zoning chapter also keeps floodplain lands 'as permanent open space' for uses and activities established after it took effect (186-46, 186-57A)

No use variance bar was found. The Zoning Hearing Board decides variances on the hardship findings of 186-101. A lot lawful when created and held in separate ownership may be built on if the yards are met (186-26). A nonconforming building may be altered or enlarged if the nonconformity does not grow (186-84)

Overlays: the Town Center Overlay (TC) over parts of R-2, C-2 and I-2 keeps the underlying uses and sets its own figures for conversions into three or more units (186-20J). The Residential Infill Overlay (RIOD) covers rowhomes only (186-20M)

Environmental standards (186-46, 186-57): at most 40% of slopes of 8% to 15%, 30% of slopes of 15% to 25% and 15% of slopes of 25% or more may be altered, cleared or built upon. Watercourses and wetlands stay permanent open space. A 100 ft buffer is kept from any wetland, with 80% of its natural cover undisturbed. At most 20% of woodland tied to another sensitive resource, and 50% of other woodland, may be cleared or built upon

term.note: Searched for in-law, accessory apartment, accessory dwelling, second dwelling, ECHO, caretaker, living quarters, guest house, garage apartment, extended family, household employee, servant, carriage house and granny, and read the use lists of every district in 186-20. No ADU use. A residential conversion may turn a house into two units or an accessory building into a unit by special exception (see the other paths)

status.note: No district lists an accessory dwelling unit. Each list permits named uses 'and no other'

path.note: A unit added to a single-family lot that is not a residential conversion is not a listed use, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board. A conversion of the house or of an accessory building is a residential conversion by special exception (see the other paths). The code does not call it an ADU

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 186-101A to E

value.name: Residential conversion of a house
value.conditions: 'The conversion of an existing building into two or more dwelling units.' A converted detached house keeps the look of a detached house with a single front entrance. Other entrances go on the side or rear, outside stairs on the rear wall, never on a front or street side wall, and there is no major structural change to the outside. Parking of 1 to 2 spaces for each unit by bedroom count, and a lot with three or more spaces is screened from the neighbors
value.note: It covers a unit made inside an existing house. In the floodplain, work on a house begun on or after March 16, 2015 is new construction, which 94-22 prohibits without a variance (94-37), and work on an older house worth 50% or more of its market value is a substantial improvement (94-33). Whether each unit needs the district's lot area per dwelling unit is not settled. 186-21 and 186-24 point to it, and 186-20J(3)(b) sets a figure per unit only for conversions into three or more units in the Town Center Overlay, which points away from it. Read per unit, two units in R-2 would need 14,000 sq ft

value.name: Residential conversion of an accessory building
value.conditions: 'The conversion of an accessory building into one or more dwelling units.' Parking of 1 to 2 spaces for each unit by bedroom count, and a lot with three or more spaces is screened from the neighbors
value.note: It covers a unit made in an existing accessory building such as a garage. In the floodplain an accessory structure may not be used for human habitation (94-22E(1)). Whether each unit needs the district's lot area per dwelling unit is not settled. 186-21 and 186-24 point to it, and 186-20J(3)(b) sets a figure per unit only for conversions into three or more units in the Town Center Overlay, which points away from it. Read per unit, two units in R-2 would need 14,000 sq ft

requires.condition: an existing accessory building to convert

value.name: Twin dwelling (R-1B, R-2, R-3, C-2)
value.conditions: Two units side by side, separated by a solid wall from ground to roof, built at the same time, each on its own lot. R-1B: 15,000 sq ft and 7,500 sq ft per unit, side yard 15 ft. R-2 and R-3: 9,000 sq ft and 4,500 per unit. C-2: 8,000 sq ft and 4,000 per unit, lot coverage 35%
value.note: A new two-unit building on two lots, not a unit added to a house. The pair needs the lot figure shown, and each twin lot the figure per unit

value.name: Duplex dwelling (R-2, R-3, C-2)
value.conditions: Two units, one over the other, separated by a solid ceiling and floor except for a common stairwell. R-2 and R-3: 9,000 sq ft and 4,500 sq ft per unit. C-2: 8,000 sq ft and 4,000 per unit, lot coverage 35%
value.note: A two-unit building. A house might become a duplex through a residential conversion (special exception)

historic_bypass.note: No historic district or historic path for a second unit was found in the parts read

districts_read_no_listing.note: None lists an accessory dwelling unit. All but I-3 list residential conversion by special exception. A, C-1, I-1, I-2 and I-3 permit no single-family dwelling. I-3 lists no special exception use (186-20L)

value.condition: 'Within any identified floodplain area, any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited' (94-22). The zoning chapter also keeps floodplain lands 'as permanent open space' (186-57A). A new building there needs a floodplain variance under Chapter 94, Article VIII, and a zoning variance.

The zoning chapter keeps floodplain lands 'as permanent open space' (186-57A), and Chapter 94 prohibits new construction and substantial improvements there (94-22). Read that way an addition built on floodplain land is barred.

disputed_by.note: For a house begun before March 16, 2015, Chapter 94 treats an addition as an improvement. It is prohibited only when it is a substantial improvement, 50% or more of the market value. Smaller work is elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible

value.condition: New construction includes any later improvement to a structure begun on or after March 16, 2015 (94-37), and 94-22 prohibits new construction in the floodplain without a variance. So work on such a house there needs a floodplain variance.
An accessory structure in the floodplain 'shall not be designed or used for human habitation' (94-22E(1)). A unit in a garage or other accessory building there would need a floodplain variance.

Work on a house begun before March 16, 2015 is an improvement. At 50% or more of the market value it is a substantial improvement, prohibited unless a variance is granted. Smaller work must be elevated or floodproofed to the greatest extent possible, and no enlargement may raise the base flood elevation.

In an AE area 'No new construction or development shall be located within the area measured 50 feet landward from the top-of-bank of any watercourse' unless DEP's regional office issues the appropriate permit. The rule is repeated for improvements to existing structures, so it reaches work on the house too.

At most 40% of slopes of 8% to 15%, 30% of slopes of 15% to 25% and 15% of slopes of 25% or more may be altered, cleared or built upon. Watercourses and wetlands stay permanent open space, and a 100 ft buffer from any wetland keeps 80% of its natural cover undisturbed.
